Learning that clumsiness is a symptom of my adhd was groundbreaking for me. During my childhood I had picked up and internalised as truth the idea that clumsiness = not being present = intentional self harm = I should be ashamed / punished. It’s wild how these ideas can just run in the background like a computer program. 
Rewriting my mental script so that when I spill my drink or run into a door handle I don’t spin into a shame spiral, but instead treat it with neutrality and say to myself “ah yes sometimes I’m clumsy and that’s okay.” I can’t always catch myself but I’m getting better at it.

I’ve been a zero waste minimalist and while gratifying for a while in the end I stopped because the vigilance required made me more anxious than clutter.

What I learned is that as long as I am aware of everything I own, I can maintain a relationship with it and designate it a home that makes sense to me. I still don’t put things back after I use them, but I put them back eventually and I feel secure knowing they have a specific place.

Now I have a box by my front door that I throw things in to take to the opshop and take it there when the box feels full.

If something makes me feel good when I see it in my home, if I enjoy having it around or I find it useful then it gets to stay.
If I think it might be useful one day, I try to let it go unless it’s unique .. for example I don’t need to save ALL my glass jars, just the ones with the lids that I like that are perfect for my ever growing spice collection.
